extracted.intended_audience: philanthropists, foundation founders, trustees, industrialists designing endowments or employee relief funds
extracted.subtask_description: Practical principles and standards for distributing large private wealth: designing endowments, relief/pension funds, libraries/institutions, governance rules, trustee selection, and employer-backed employee benefits. Emphasis on durable public benefit and prudent administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief fund design for accidents and pensions
rubrics_metrics.description: "I make this first use of surplus wealth, four millions of first mortgage 5% Bonds, ... It is designed to relieve those who may suffer from accidents, and provide small pensions for those needing help in old age."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design relief/endowment funds with explicit, limited purposes (accident relief and small pensions). Provide concrete mechanism (bonds) and state intended beneficiaries. Example: Andrew Carnegie's 'Andrew Carnegie Relief Fund' for employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use endowed income to maintain built facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: "In addition I give one million dollars of such bonds, the proceeds thereof to be used to maintain the libraries and halls I have built for our workmen."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate capital from operating funds: endow the maintenance (income/proceeds) of buildings and institutions rather than relying on capital depletion. Specify the use of proceeds in the gift instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad but specific mission in deed of gift
rubrics_metrics.description: "To encourage in the broadest and most liberal manner investigations, research and discovery, and the application of knowledge to the improvement of mankind; and, in particular, to conduct, endow and assist investigation in any department of science, literature or art..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State a broad overarching mission while listing concrete activities (conduct, endow, assist investigations). A broad mission allows flexibility but should be tied to actionable domains and cooperating institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of hero/recognition funds: pension/support, not incentive
rubrics_metrics.description: "The fund is intended to pension or provide in the most suitable manner for the hero should he be disabled, or for those dependent upon him should he perish in his attempt to save others... Many thought that its purpose was to stimulate heroic action... This never entered my mind. It is absurd. True heroes think not of reward."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design awards/funds to provide relief or support for exceptional service, not to create perverse incentives. Clearly articulate that the fund's role is remedial/pensionary, not a reward-for-risk inducement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select distinguished, capable trustees and leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: consulting President Roosevelt, asking John Hay to serve as chairman, appointing Dr. Daniel C. Gilman and Dr. Robert S. Woodward as presidents; "I found the president for the Hero Fund in a Carnegie veteran... He is the right man in the right place."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit reputable, competent, and committed individuals as trustees and executive officers. Prefer those with relevant experience and devotion to the mission; leadership quality can outweigh salary considerations (some leaders may serve without pay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include governance flexibility (trustees may change objectives) with supermajority
rubrics_metrics.description: "I had proposed that a majority should have the power, but Lord Balfour suggested not less than two thirds. This was accepted by the Earl of Elgin and approved by all. ... It is incorporated in all my large gifts..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate a clause granting trustees the power to alter objects/modes of beneficence if circumstances render original provisions unsuitable, and require a supermajority (recommended two-thirds) to do so. This preserves adaptability for future generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against misuse; exercise care in administration
rubrics_metrics.description: "Scarcely less admirable than the gifts themselves is the great care and thought you have taken in guarding against their misuse."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build administrative safeguards, careful selection of trustees, and oversight mechanisms into gift instruments to prevent misapplication of funds. Emphasize prudence and attention to long-term stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate with governments, universities, learned societies and individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: "...to coöperate with governments, universities, colleges, technical schools, learned societies, and individuals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design institutions to partner and coordinate with public bodies and existing learned institutions to amplify impact and legitimacy. Use cooperation clauses and invitations to distinguished partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize smaller institutions and underfunded beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: "My belief was that our chief universities, such as Harvard and Columbia, with five to ten thousand students, were large enough; that further growth was undesirable; that the smaller institutions (the colleges especially) were in greater need of help and that it would be a better use of surplus wealth to aid them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target philanthropic resources to institutions or sectors with greater marginal need (smaller colleges, underpaid professions) rather than to already well-endowed large institutions to maximize social benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish pensions to retain and support deserving professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: "The fifteen-million-dollar pension fund for aged university professors... Educated men, devoting their lives to teaching the young, receive mere pittances... To save for old age with these men is impossible. Hence the universities without pension funds are compelled to retain men who are no longer able..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use endowments to create pension funds for undervalued professionals (e.g., professors) to ensure institutions can retain effective staff and avoid keeping unfit personnel due to lack of retirement support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use endowments to expand public access to knowledge and civic institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: giving branch libraries for New York City and Brooklyn, a public library and hall to Allegheny City, establishment of a group in Pittsburgh embracing a museum, picture gallery, technical schools, and a school for young women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund publicly accessible cultural and educational infrastructure (libraries, museums, technical schools) to promote broad civic benefit. Prioritize branch and local access to reach working communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endow with durable instruments and specify sustainable funding (bonds, income streams)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnegie's gifts often used first mortgage 5% bonds and directed "the proceeds thereof" for maintenance and ongoing support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide durable capital (e.g., bonds or invested endowment) and explicitly earmark income/proceeds for ongoing operations to ensure sustainability rather than one-time spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate internationally and exchange administrative reports
rubrics_metrics.description: "They have corresponded with the English and French Commission, arranged to exchange reports, and made plans to keep in touch with one another in their work."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage cross-jurisdictional learning and sharing of administrative reports among equivalent funds/commissions to improve decision-making and harmonize best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid personal profit from philanthropic transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: "There had been so much deception by speculators ... that I declined to take anything for the common stock. Had I done so, it would have given me just about one hundred millions more... But I had enough..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from structuring gifts that result in personal enrichment or unfair private gain tied to philanthropic actions. Maintain ethical separation between private financial advantage and charitable distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design practical, problem-focused employee support measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: establishing a coöperative store (men take stock and manage it), company selling coal to employees at net cost and arranging delivery, accepting workers' savings up to two thousand dollars and paying six per cent and lending for home building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement pragmatic, locally-relevant benefits (cooperatives, in-kind cost reductions, trusted savings schemes and housing loans) to address workers' concrete needs and build mutual trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate aims clearly to prevent misconceptions about incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding the Hero Fund: "A strange misconception arose at first about it. Many thought that its purpose was to stimulate heroic action... To-day we have in America 1430 hero pensioners or their families on our list... as its aims and services are better understood."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively communicate the purpose and limitations of funds to the public and press to prevent misinterpretation of intent (e.g., that a pension fund is not a bounty to induce risk-taking). Public reporting and clear annual reports help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor reconciliation and humane treatment in employer-employee relations
rubrics_metrics.description: "Suits had been entered against many of the strikers, but upon my return these were promptly dismissed. All the old men who remained, and had not been guilty of violence, were taken back."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing employer-supported relief or philanthropic responses to labor disputes, prefer reconciliation, reintegration, and humane remedies over punitive legal actions to restore trust and community.
